Controls.Text:
2026-11-14 01:05 Developer: Hi Daniel, we are about to install a new Velocity9x display driver build on this PC (the first with GeForce 210 2D acceleration) and restart it. The old files are backed up. If the screen does not come back after the restart, please power-cycle; if it is still wrong, start in Safe Mode and tell us. Thank you.
2026-11-14 01:18 Developer: Hi Daniel, the new driver is installed and running on this PC: the GeForce 210 now does DirectDraw fills and copies on its own 2D engine, and our tests passed. If you notice anything odd on screen (wrong colours, garbage, flicker), please tell us here. Thank you for all your help with this card.
2026-11-14 02:58 Developer: Hi Daniel, we are about to install a newer Velocity9x build on this PC and restart it. This one also draws the Windows desktop (window fills and scrolling) on the GeForce 210's 2D engine. The current files are backed up first. If the screen does not come back, please power-cycle; if the desktop looks wrong (garbage, wrong colours, windows not redrawing), please tell us here. Thank you.
2026-11-14 06:49 Developer: Hi Daniel, thank you, the PC is back. Did you power-cycle it, and if so, what was on the screen before you did (frozen desktop, black screen, Windows logo)? We are now installing one more build and restarting it once; then we run short tests. If it does not come back, a power-cycle is fine as before.
2026-11-14 06:50 You: It had froze on the Windows logo boot screen
2026-11-14 07:12 Developer: Hi Daniel, testing is done for now. The GeForce 210 now draws parts of the Windows desktop on its own 2D engine, but after a few hundred operations one of them stalls, and the driver then switches back to drawing everything with the CPU, as designed. The desktop should look normal. If you see anything odd on screen, please tell us. Thank you.
2026-11-14 07:51 Developer: Hi Daniel, thanks for the power-cycle and for telling us it froze on the Windows boot screen; that helps. We are installing one more test build now and restarting the PC once, then running short tests. If it does not come back, a power-cycle is fine as before.
2026-11-14 08:25 Developer: Hi Daniel, good news: the GeForce 210 now draws Windows desktop fills and scrolling on its own 2D engine, and all our tests pass. The stall we mentioned earlier turned out to be our own test tool, not the driver. Testing is done for now. If you see anything odd on screen (garbage, wrong colours, windows not redrawing), please tell us. Thank you!
2026-11-14 08:33 Developer: Hi Daniel, one more quick check: we are installing the same driver again, now combined with our main version, and restarting the PC once for a few minutes of tests. If it does not come back, a power-cycle is fine. Thank you.
2026-11-14 09:43 Developer: Hi Daniel, we are starting work on 3D for the GeForce 210. In the next few minutes we will restart the PC once and run a short test of the card's 3D engine (nothing is drawn on screen). A first 3D test carries a small chance of a freeze; if it happens, a power-cycle fixes it as before. Thank you!
2026-11-15 12:02 You: hi, I have an issue with Quake 3 on the GeForce 210. When I start the game either a static corrupted or black image are shown. Happens both in window and fullscreen. The game doesn't crash as I can still hear the sounds from it.
2026-11-15 12:15 You: Looks like there's a similar issue with Quake II and after terminating the game this error message are shown in a small window "GLimp_EndFrame() - SwapBuffers() failed"
2026-11-15 13:41 Developer: Thanks for the reports, I'm doing a major update for the Geforce 210 soon, please keep this machine on and I will keep you updated.
2026-11-15 14:11 Developer: Hi Daniel, we found why Quake 3 and Quake II showed a black or frozen picture on the GeForce 210: the OpenGL driver never handed its textures to the card, and the card had no fallback, so nothing textured was drawn.
